author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
Follow-up to #2001. That PR restored a pushable git remote, but autoheal fixes still had nowhere to land — the credential was never the binding constraint.

## The actual rule

`fro-bot/agent` resolves delivery mode from one action input:

```ts
resolveOutputMode(eventType, configuredMode)
```

For `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`:

| configured | resolved |
| --- | --- |
| `working-dir` | `working-dir` |
| `branch-pr` | `branch-pr` |
| `auto` (default) | **`working-dir`** |

Every other event type returns `null` and ignores the input entirely.

The resolver takes no credential, actor, or filesystem input. An on-disk `extraheader` has no bearing on the result. `action.yaml` states it directly:

> Manual auto requests always resolve to working-dir; use branch-pr explicitly when branch/PR delivery is required.

Source: [`packages/runtime/src/agent/output-mode.ts`](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/blob/main/packages/runtime/src/agent/output-mode.ts)

## Why this was missed

This workflow never set `output-mode`, so it fell through to the `auto` compatibility default and resolved to `working-dir` on every run — schedule and dispatch alike.

The daily autohealing report (#1665) attributed the failure to a missing credential step, citing `marcusrbrown/mrbro.dev` as having the fix. That difference was real, and #2001 ported it. But `mrbro.dev` does not set `output-mode` either, so it resolves to `working-dir` too. The comparison found a genuine difference between the repos and attributed causation to it without establishing that it was the operative one.

#2001 remains a prerequisite — once `branch-pr` is active the agent needs a credential to actually push — but it was not sufficient on its own.

## Change

Requests `branch-pr` explicitly for the paths that need to deliver fixes: [description truncated to fit budget]
title: fix(ci): request branch-pr delivery for Fro Bot autoheal runs
